fields.acceptance: A Go test finds the process in the journal of a started run and of a resumed one, and a reader reports a fixture's unfinished journal as live and interrupted when its pid is not running, as live and running when it is the test's own process, and a finished journal as not live.
fields.statement: A run journals its process (host and pid) when it starts and each time it is resumed, so a reader tells which of the live runs (unfinished journals, as run-one-live counts them) are running and which are interrupted: an unfinished journal whose process is gone.

fields.acceptance: A Go test over a fixture model with two accepted milestone change sets with leaves, an accepted leafless milestone change set, an accepted backlog change set with leaves, one running run on a third accepted milestone change set and one interrupted run on a fourth picks only the first milestone change set under max 2, and none under max 1; a testscript runs rhiza daemon --once with a fake Rex and sees that one start.
fields.statement: Each poll, the daemon picks the accepted change sets that rhiza ready says can start, that serve a milestone intent, have at least one leaf and have no live run (running or interrupted, as run-one-live counts it), in roadmap order, and starts them until its running runs (live runs whose process is running) reach --max-runs (default 2), so an interrupted run keeps its change set from being picked but takes no slot; it never starts a backlog, draft, proposed or leafless change set.

fields.acceptance: A testscript with a fixture journal that is unfinished and names a dead process runs rhiza daemon --once twice with a fake Rex: the first opens one tab running rhiza run resume on that run and journals it, the second (with the run interrupted again) opens none; a failed run's journal gets no tab.
fields.statement: The daemon resumes an interrupted run once, as rhiza run resume <run> in a new Rex tab, and journals that resume in the run's journal; it leaves alone a run interrupted again after that resume, which the inbox lists as a run the daemon gave up on, and every failed run, which the inbox lists as failed.
